finding.claim: subscribe() stores an unvalidated, attacker-supplied callbackUrl; notifyAll() later POSTs the payload to it on a recurring schedule, enabling blind server-side request forgery to arbitrary internal or external http(s) hosts.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of Jobs.subscribe (src/Jobs.java:13), documented as the body of POST /subscribe (src/Jobs.java:12)
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) issuing an HTTP POST to URI.create(cb) (src/Jobs.java:21-24)

trace.note: Comment documents callbackUrl as a request body field of POST /subscribe
subscribe(name, callbackUrl) accepts the raw string
Stored unchanged in static subscriptions map
Iterates over all stored callback values
URI.create(cb) converts the attacker string to a URI with no checks
client.send issues the request; response body discarded

finding.guards_checked: No validation in subscribe() (no scheme, host, IP, or port allowlist). No validation in notifyAll(). No request timeout set. HttpClient.newHttpClient() uses default Redirect.NEVER, so redirects are not followed. HttpRequest.Builder.uri rejects non-http(s) schemes, so file: and similar are unreachable. http/https to loopback, RFC1918, and link-local (e.g. 169.254.169.254) are reachable. Authentication on /subscribe is not in this repository and could not be verified. Severity is blind (response not returned), but internal POST-accepting services and timing or error oracles remain reachable. Checked and cleared: Jobs.thumb (src/Jobs.java:29-34) is not a finding: String.matches full-match regex at line 30 fixes host to cdn.example.com with no userinfo, path traversal, query, or fragment injection, and redirects are not followed.

verdict.guard_found: none in src/Jobs.java: subscribe() (src/Jobs.java:13-15) stores callbackUrl unchanged and notifyAll() (src/Jobs.java:18-25) calls URI.create(cb) with no checks; the only other file-local check is the thumb() regex at src/Jobs.java:30, which is not on this path.
verdict.reason: Every trace line (src/Jobs.java:12, 13, 14, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24) exists and matches the claim, and no guard closes the sink at src/Jobs.java:21, but the only evidence that callbackUrl is remotely attacker-controlled is the comment at src/Jobs.java:12 saying it is the body of POST /subscribe, and the route wiring and auth for /subscribe are not in this repository (grep finds no router or caller), so exposure to an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot be verified.
